{"magic":"0x74","magic_offset":0,"notes":"This burst IS the readback protocol (frame.readback) -- the Launcher walking every (category, index). Decoded 2026-08-31: the host SENDS a 0x74 request `74 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 <cat> 00 00 00 <idx> 00 00 00` on EP 0x01 OUT and the device REPLIES with `75 00 00 00 40 01 00 00 <cat> ... <idx> ... <data>` on EP 0x82 IN. It is not names-only and not one-shot -- it carries live state (routing = cat 0x03, mixer = cat 0x04, AuraVerb = cat 0x0a, ...). The text below is the original (pre-decode) analysis of the connect burst, kept for the emission-order detail. A one-shot device topology enumeration. Seen ONLY in all_reports_AntelopeINIT.tsv (113 records, t=7.5-16s of the connect sequence), never in any other capture. That capture is the Antelope Launcher being launched with NO user interaction (confirmed by the user) -- so this whole burst, and the single outgoing 0x70/SET_PARAM(param 0x49) at t=7.71s, is the Launcher's automatic startup/handshake, not anything a user did. Full emission order (see PROTOCOL.md section 4): 0x11 x2 (S/PDIF); 0x0b marker; 0x1b x1 singleton; 0x1a x16 (ADAT -- confirmed); 0x03 x15 (unmapped); 0x04 x4 (unmapped, each entry trailed by its own 0x0b=3 marker); 0x0a x1, 0x15 x1, 0x16 x1 singletons; 0x19 x64 (unmapped -- almost certainly the 64-channel USB/Thunderbolt stream, the device's headline I/O count; routing command's first payload byte 0x41=65 is consistent with a 1-based index into a 64-entry space); 0x0b closing markers. 0x0b (8 records, index values 1/2/3/3/3/3/0/4) is a section/phase marker, NOT an I/O category. Confirmed: 0x1a=ADAT, 0x11=S/PDIF. Still unnamed: 0x19/0x03/0x04 and the four singletons. NOTE (2026-08): checked all 21 raw pcapng files -- NOT ONE contains a USB string-descriptor fetch, and the UAC2 descriptor is a stub with no channel names. So the names are Launcher-internal and cannot be recovered from any capture on file; the practical routes are (a) a fresh connect capture where Windows re-fetches string descriptors, or (b) reading the counts off against the Launcher's routing-tab labels. This is NOT a live settings readback -- indices only, no current values. Listed here mainly so scan tools stop flagging 0x74 as unknown. CROSS-PLATFORM CONFIRMED (2026-08): the four native-macOS INIT captures (macos-antelopeINIT-*) reproduce this exactly -- same 0x74 burst (byte-identical between captures with different device state), and the SAME single outgoing handshake frame SET_PARAM(param 0x49, channel 1, value 0). That one 0x49 frame is the ENTIRE host->device connect handshake; everything else the Launcher does at connect is either passive polling or cosmetic state restore (a SET_PARAM(gain 0x50) fade-in ramp). macOS capture layout: 40-byte Darwin pseudo-header + 320-byte payload (frame.len==360), payload byte 0 = magic; 0x74 arrives on IN endpoint 1, 0x73/0x75 on IN endpoint 2.","record_layout":"header 0x74, u32 constant 0x10 @4, u32 category_id @8, u32 index @12 (0-based, 0..count-1 within a category); nothing non-zero past offset 16. Records carry (category_id, index) ONLY -- no names (names would be USB string descriptors, i.e. control transfers, not in the 320-byte HID capture).","status":"unconfirmed"}

hazards.name: channel_index_out_of_range
hazards.notes: Orion's CLI currently only warns past channels.confirmed_indices and sends anyway. Given the sibling behaviour that is too loose -- an out-of-range write should be refused unless --force. The same byte carries bus ids for bus params, where 0-5 are legal, so a single global channel-count check is wrong.

One frame per (mix, channel) strip, carrying that strip's WHOLE state every time. CONFIRMED from macos-mix1-send-pan-fader-mute-solo-link (2026-08, native macOS): [16]=0xd4 [17]=0x05 constant; [18]=mix number 0-3 (0 = Mix 1 .. 3 = Mix 4) -- CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 via the cat-0x04 readback, which returns an independent record for each of the four indices (the original capture had only ever shown mix 0); [19]=channel **0-32**: 1-32 = the input strips (each mix has 32 -- the user's solo click re-sent all 32, a handy channel-count probe) and **0 = the MIX MASTER strip** (CONFIRMED 2026-09-01 from captures/new/mix1-masterfaderplay.pcapng: sweeping the Mix 1 master fader emits 68 frames, all `d4 05 00 00 <fader> 20 60` -- channel 0, pan/send held constant. No target byte past 22. READBACK: frame.readback category 0x04, index = mix number 0..3 -- FULLY DECODED + hardware round-trip verified 2026-08-31. That round trip also confirmed [18] really is the mix number (all four mixes return their own record) and that [22] is stored send state, not a meter. protocol.parse_mixer_record; CLI `mix-status`. Also category 0x1b = mixer bus level/range table (still undecoded). transport.notes: Confirmed from raw pcapng (2026-08): the vendor control protocol is entirely HID interrupt on interface 3, endpoint 0x01 OUT / 0x82 IN, device address 2 (usb.dst 1.2.x). Endpoints 0x05 OUT / 0x84 IN are the UAC2 isochronous audio stream (24-ch / 24-bit in the class-compliant descriptor) -- unrelated to control. Only 16 USB control transfers in the whole connect sequence: standard descriptor GETs + SET_CONFIGURATION/SET_INTERFACE, NO string-descriptor fetches in any capture on file. The UAC2 audio-control descriptor is a stub (1 clock source, 4 terminals all nrChannels=1, no Feature Units), so it carries no usable channel topology or names.
